themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints skyrocketed to 17 THIS WEEK, up 3,300% from a baseline of 0.5 complaints per week over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 23.33), suggesting a coordinated campaign or sudden enforcement gap in Ridgewood/Glendale/Middle Village.
evidence: 17 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 23.33 indicates extreme statistical outlier
Peak concentration suggests localized problem rather than district-wide trend
reporting_angles: Walk the district to document where illegal postings are concentrated and what they advertise
Investigate whether Community Board or local merchants have reported a specific campaign (illegal gambling, unlicensed services, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Pigeon Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary pigeon condition complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, a 700% increase from the 8-week baseline of 0.5 per week (z-score: 4.95), pointing to a acute public health concern in a specific neighborhood pocket.
evidence: 4 unsanitary pigeon complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average
Concurrent spike in street sign damage (9 complaints this week, +300%) may indicate physical debris or deterioration attracting birds
reporting_angles: Interview residents in affected blocks about health concerns and property damage from pigeon droppings
Investigate whether local restaurants or food vendors have inadequate waste management that attracts pigeons

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints surged to 16 LAST WEEK, up 198% from the 8-week baseline of 5.4 per week (z-score: 3.82), with concurrent spikes in damaged street signs (9 THIS WEEK, +300%) suggesting accelerating street deterioration across the district.
evidence: 16 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (+198%)
9 damaged street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average (+300%)
5 missing street signs LAST WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average (+186%)
Community Board has repeatedly requested DEP sewer inspection and repair on specific street segments (unfunded for multiple years)
reporting_angles: Map the locations of root damage, sewer complaints, and missing/damaged signs to identify whether a single street or corridor is failing
Interview residents about trip hazards, flooding, or code violations from sidewalk damage and investigate why CB's long-standing DEP budget request remains unfunded

themes_detail.label: Emergency Response Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Emergency Response Team (ERT) complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, a 380% increase from the 8-week baseline of 0.6 per week (z-score: 4.91), indicating a possible public safety incident cluster or policing pattern change in the district.
evidence: 3 ERT complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over 8 weeks (+380%)
ERT typically deployed for violent crime, gang activity, or high-risk incidents
Spike is sudden and concentrated in single week
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD public information to determine what incident(s) triggered ERT deployments last week
Canvass residents and local merchants in the areas where ERT was called to understand the context and any ongoing safety concerns

themes_detail.label: Animal Nuisance Pattern Shift
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal private property complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 300% from the 8-week baseline of 0.8 per week (z-score: 5.2), paired with concurrent pigeon infestation spike, suggesting an emerging animal control or waste management problem.
evidence: 3 unsanitary animal complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly average over 8 weeks (+300%)
Concurrent 700% spike in pigeon infestation complaints suggests related root cause (food waste exposure, inadequate sanitation)
Pattern may be early warning of district-wide waste management degradation
reporting_angles: Interview animal control to see whether complaints involve rodents, loose pets, or other species and whether there's a geographic cluster
Investigate whether trash collection schedules have changed or bin capacity is inadequate for residential density
